title: Invertibility and one-input refinement equation for explicit support reduction
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a coefficient datum C with prime ℓ distinct from the characteristic, a finite extension E of Q_ℓ, n≥1, and a normalized six-functor operation datum S at n. Assume ℓ is invertible in D.k. Let o be simultaneous-system operations and z their canonical realization data. Let f:X→Y be separated, locally of finite type and quasi-compact between finite-type schemes over D.k. For every compactification c=(j_c,p_c) of f and every constructible integral object K on X, the actual supportReduction(c,K) of [def-sf-integral-projection-coordinate-data] from reduction of S.integral.support(f,c)(K) to S_p_c J_j_c(reduction K) is invertible. For every refinement r:c→d, supportReduction(d,K) followed by the directed systemComparison(r,reduction K) equals reduction of the inverse datum compactification comparison at K followed by supportReduction(c,K). This is an identity of simultaneous coefficient-system maps, with no tensor, projection map or existential choice of coordinates.

proof.text: Use constructibleReduction_good for the input, then openSupportStep_bounds for the compactification open, then properSupportStep_bounds for its proper map. These three proved declarations give Good input, Good intermediate open output and Good support output, including normalization and the common finite bounds. The normalized reconstruction theorem makes the actual support counit invertible. The defining support adjunct is reduction of supportValue inverse followed by that counit, hence invertible.

proof.text: Transport the directed systemComparison through the two supportValue isomorphisms to an actual morphism a between integral constructible outputs. Naturality of the reconstruction counit proves the supportReduction square with a. At each finite quotient use the support-adjunct coordinates and the single-level refinement coordinates to compute reduction of a. Invert the coefficient-comparison compactification square to identify this with reduction of the inverse datum comparison. The proved Milnor joint-faithfulness theorem on integral constructible objects identifies a with that comparison. Substitute into the counit square. No faithfulness of arbitrary derived-system evaluation is used.

theorem integralSupportReductionNormalization
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (C : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (S : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn) (hl : IsUnit (C.l : D.k))
    (o : Operations C.l E) (z : Realizations C.l E D o)
    {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsSeparated f.hom.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.hom.left] [QuasiCompact f.hom.left] :
    (∀ (c : Compactification f.hom.left)
      (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E X.obj.left),
      IsIso (Coordinates.supportReduction D C E S.higher hl o z f c K)) ∧
    (∀ (c d : Compactification f.hom.left) (r : c.Refinement d)
      (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E X.obj.left),
      Coordinates.supportReduction D C E S.higher hl o z f d K ≫
          RefinementProjection.systemComparison C.l E D o z r
            ((calculus C.l E X.obj.left).reduction.obj K.obj) =
        (calculus C.l E Y.obj.left).reduction.map
          (((S.higher.integral.comparison f c d).inv.app K).hom) ≫
            Coordinates.supportReduction D C E S.higher hl o z f c K)
